subsection: 3. Developments over the past twenty years

notes.b: Three developments have changed opportunities for women in sport.
points: Development 1, visibility: the 20x20 campaign, launched in 2018, and more televised women's Gaelic games, rugby and soccer.
Impact of visibility: girls see women playing sport on mainstream channels, which gives them role models to follow.
Development 2, pay and Olympic success: in 2021 the FAI announced equal match payments for Ireland's senior women's and men's international teams.
Development 2, Olympic success: women's boxing was first included at the London 2012 Olympics, where Katie Taylor won gold.
Impact of pay and Olympic success: equal match payments signal equal status for women's and men's international players, and Olympic success gives women's sport a high profile.
Development 3, policy and leadership: Sport Ireland's Women in Sport policy and funding, and more female coaches and administrators.
Impact of policy and leadership: targeted funding and female coaches and administrators give women's sport its own structures and visible leaders.
Still to change: unequal pay and resources across sports, and too few women in senior coaching and administration.

notes.b: Three developments have widened the options for older adults.
points: Development 1: Go for Life, the national programme for sport and physical activity for older people, run by Age & Opportunity with Sport Ireland support.
Impact of Go for Life: older adults have a national structure of programmes designed for their age and ability.
Development 2: growth of walking groups, parkrun and masters competitions.
Impact of walking groups and events: older adults can join in at their own pace, from a casual walk to a competitive event.
Development 3: age-friendly gym classes and 'get active' initiatives.
Impact of gym classes: classes built for older adults challenge the stereotype that they are too frail for strength training.
Still to change: stereotypes about ageing, and the limited coverage of older adults' sport in the media.

notes.b: Three developments have changed opportunities for people with physical disability.
points: Development 1: growth of the Paralympic Games and Irish success there.
Impact of Paralympic growth: Paralympic success gives disabled athletes visible role models and raises the profile of disability sport.
Development 2: Sports Inclusion Disability Officers in Local Sports Partnerships, who help local clubs and schools include disabled people.
Impact of the officers: clubs and schools have local advice on adapting activities and welcoming disabled people.
Development 3: more accessible facilities, and wheelchair and adapted versions of mainstream sports.
Impact of adapted versions: wheelchair basketball and similar sports let people play in forms that suit their impairment.
Still to change: accessibility of facilities and transport, the supply of adapted equipment, and the number of trained coaches.

notes.b: Developments for people with intellectual disability centre on a major international event, growing club provision and unified sport.
points: Context from before the twenty-year window: the Special Olympics World Summer Games were held in Dublin in 2003, the first held outside the United States.
Impact of the 2003 Games: they gave Special Olympics sport a high profile in Ireland.
Development 1: growth of Special Olympics clubs and inclusive club sessions.
Impact of clubs: more clubs give people with intellectual disability regular, local places to train and compete.
Development 2: unified sports, in which people with and without intellectual disability play on the same teams.
Impact of unified sports: players with intellectual disability take full team roles alongside peers without disability.
Still to change: coach training, the low expectations held by some coaches, and the limited number of programmes.

notes.b: Three developments have made sport more open to players from different backgrounds.
points: Development 1: a more diverse population taking part in Irish and international sports.
Impact of diversity: clubs and national teams draw on players from more backgrounds, which widens the role models on show.
Development 2: anti-racism education and campaigns by national governing bodies (NGBs) and Sport Against Racism Ireland (SARI).
Impact of anti-racism work: education for players, coaches and officials challenges racism and prejudice in sport.
Development 3: inclusive dress rules that allow players to wear religious and cultural clothing.
Impact of dress rules: players can take part without giving up religious or cultural dress.
Still to change: racism and stereotyping in clubs and crowds, and the lack of role models from some backgrounds.

notes.b: Three developments have put free or low-cost activity within reach of people on lower incomes.
points: Development 1: free mass-participation events such as parkrun, which is free and weekly.
Impact of parkrun: anyone can join a free weekly event whatever their income.
Development 2: Local Sports Partnership programmes in disadvantaged areas.
Impact of Local Sports Partnership programmes: activity is targeted at areas where income and local facilities are limited.
Development 3: outdoor gyms, greenways and other public facilities.
Impact of public facilities: free public spaces give people somewhere to be active without membership fees.
Still to change: club fees, kit and travel costs, and gaps in local facilities.

questions.prompt: Discuss two developments in physical activity and sport over the past twenty years for one group of your choice and their impact.
questions.model: Group: women. Development 1: the 20x20 campaign, launched in 2018 to increase the visibility of women's sport in Ireland. Its impact is that girls and women see women playing and coaching, which gives them role models and makes participation seem possible. Development 2: women's boxing was first included at the London 2012 Olympics, where Katie Taylor won gold. Its impact is that women's boxing reached the highest level of competition and gave women's sport a high profile at a major event. Both developments raised the visibility of women's sport, but unequal pay and resources across sports, and too few women in senior coaching and administration, still need to change.

questions.prompt: Describe one development in sport over the past twenty years for women and outline its impact.
questions.model: Development: in 2021 the FAI announced equal match payments for Ireland's senior women's and men's international teams. Impact: women's international players receive the same match payments as men's, which signals that women's sport is valued equally. It gives women's players fair recognition for their work and can encourage girls to see international football as a serious sporting path.
